gates.notes: generateCandidates returns starts in chronological order, deduplicated by instant (Set in dayGridStarts), so each batch is strictly increasing and batches are consecutive slices of one global sequence. The first free candidate of the earliest batch is therefore the globally earliest free slot.

Next batch starts at last.start + 1 ms and generateCandidates keeps start >= from, so the previous last start is excluded and every later start is included. Grid starts sit on whole minutes, so 1 ms cannot skip a candidate. The day containing the batch boundary is regenerated and filtered by start >= from, so no candidate is dropped or repeated. The DST repeated hour is handled because the boundary is an instant, not a wall-clock time.

Loop condition from < horizonEnd; every iteration that continues has a full batch (batch.length === limit) and advances from by at least 1 ms; an empty or short batch returns null (generateCandidates stops at limit, so a short batch means the horizon is exhausted). Bound: one batch per 2000 candidates, about 5 batches for a full 365-day hourly grid at 24 h/day (the practical maximum), each at most 2 reads. maxDaysAhead is validated to at most 365.

horizonEnd is fixed once (max(startFrom, now) + maxDaysAhead days) and each batch passes (horizonEnd - from) / day as maxDaysAhead, so the original horizon is preserved across batches. The division and multiplication can differ by a sub-millisecond float error at the exclusive boundary instant only; no practical effect. Day scan uses maxDaysAhead + 1 margin, covering DST-length days.

Each batch reads CAP_COUNTED_STATUSES appointments (tenantId-scoped) over [local day start of its first candidate, local day end of its last candidate), i.e. whole firm-local days. A day split across two batches is therefore counted in full in both, so the per-day count is identical regardless of where the batch boundary falls. An all-capped batch returns null and the loop continues to the next batch rather than ending the search.

Prior LOW finding resolved: findNextSlotWithinAvailability throws PRECONDITION_FAILED with the shared INVALID_TIMEZONE_MESSAGE (now exported from the domain) before any read, matching create and reschedule. A test pins code, message and that the conflict use case is not called.
Prior LOW finding resolved: schema.prisma now differs from main by 58 added / 21 removed lines (PG-202 changes only). Migration and models unchanged since the first verdict.

Number.parseInt, getLocalHour default parameter (timezone = 'UTC'; legacy callers pass undefined so the result is identical) and dropping async from two settings mutations that return the Prisma promise are behaviour-preserving. The findNextSlot router no longer logs the search; the return shape { slot, searchDurationMs } is unchanged.
The only domain change is exporting an existing string constant. No new imports in domain or application; no container wiring change.
At review time summary.tsv held rows 01-03 only (all exit 0, started 2026-10-18T09:00:51Z) and no 'done' marker, so rows 04 onward were not yet available. This verdict does not rely on them.

findings.issue: The batching test asserts two batches, a first batch of exactly 2000 and that the second batch starts after the first batch's last start. It does not assert the 1 ms boundary exactly or the cap behaviour across a split day, which this review verified by reading only.
findings.fix: Optionally add a case with a daily cap whose day straddles the batch boundary, and assert second[0] is the first start strictly after first[1999].

findings.issue: Each batch regenerates the boundary day and recomputes cap and conflict windows; a worst case search with no free slot does about 5 batches x 2 reads. Bounded and acceptable.

limitations: Read-only review: no tests, typecheck, lint, build or depcruise were run. The full matrix at 2ac93b60f was still running (rows 01-03 only, no 'done'), so no log from it was used; the earlier logs at 1cd895b72 are not evidence for the new code. Domain semantics of the batching were judged from the source and the added unit test. The depcruise boundary gate and the migrate-diff confirmation remain without logs, as in the first verdict.
